newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures rally to end mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures rally to end mostly higher.

text.p: CME lumber futures rallied from a near-limit decline of $9.90 per thousand board feet in March early to end mostly higher with only March still holding a loss at the close, traders said.
Lumber closed $0.90 per tbf lower to $4.20 higher with only March off at $400.50 and May up most at $379.50.
Short covering, partly prompted by reduced concern over increased Canadian lumber exports before the end of the quota year, boosted futures late, traders said.
Ronald McDonald, parliamentary secretary to Canada's International Trade Minister Art Eggleton, clarified lumber export rules under the five-year agreement.
McDonald said mills not using their quota could give the remaining part of their quota back and this would protect their quota in next year equasion,

"Obviously, players in the U.S., as to the disposition of unused quota, have misinterpreted that mills have to ship fully up to quota levels in order not to jeopardize their next year's quota, when in fact this is not the case," said Gerry Yane with Marleau Lemire Inc in Montreal.
"This should take away a negative in futures", he said.
But weak cash and bear spreading weighed on March futures. "There's still a lot of lumber around," Yane added.

The U.S. Commerce Department's December single-family new home sales report, which showed sales down one percent at 783,000 units compared with the previous month, was above Wall Street economists' expectations for a 3-1/2 percent decline. The news was slightly supportive to lumber futures initially. Overall, the data showed new home sales in 1996 were the strongest in 18 years.
